scope: Deterministic validation rules that cannot be guaranteed by JSON Schema alone. This registry is not an executable validator and no Runtime claim is made.

duplicate_edge_policy.semantic_key: relation_type plus canonical endpoints plus canonical condition_refs
duplicate_edge_policy.symmetric_endpoint_normalization: sort endpoint IDs when relation registry marks relation symmetric
duplicate_edge_policy.condition_refs_semantics: all listed conditions apply conjunctively (AND) in v1; OR alternatives must use distinct edges with distinct condition sets
duplicate_edge_policy.provenance_handling: different provenance alone does not make a distinct edge; merge source refs only after human confirmation
duplicate_edge_policy.attribute_conflicts: do not auto-merge different attributes; report conflict for human resolution

defaults.mixed_relation_cycle_policy: warn_in_v1; publication requires the exact cycle path and explicit human acknowledgement in release record; do not infer a forbidden cycle unless a combined constraint is registered
defaults.cycle_warning_policy: cycles with cycle_policy warn may remain in drafts; published releases must include the exact warning paths and an explicit human acknowledgement in the release record

rules.condition: Input is not valid JSON
Input does not validate against the pinned JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 contract
The schema's relation_type enum differs from the selected relation registry keys, or the selected rule profile is unavailable
An id is duplicated across nodes, edges, conditions, or sources
An edge source_id or target_id does not resolve to an id in nodes
A provenance_refs entry does not resolve to an id in sources
A condition_refs entry does not resolve to an id in conditions
An edge creates a self-loop where source_id equals target_id

Two edges have the same semantic key: relation_type plus canonical endpoints plus canonicalized condition_refs; endpoints are normalized for symmetric relations. condition_refs is interpreted conjunctively in v1. Different provenance alone does not distinguish an edge.
rules.action: block_publish_and_report_duplicate_edges; recommend human-reviewed merge of provenance; never auto-merge attributes

rules.condition: An edge, condition, or source reference is retained after its referenced object was deleted
A cycle exists in a relation_type whose cycle_policy is forbidden, considering only edges of that relation_type
A cycle exists in a relation_type whose cycle_policy is warn
rules.action: allow_draft_and_warn; published release requires warning path plus explicit reviewer acknowledgement in release record

rules.condition: A mixed-relation cycle contains more than one relation_type but no single relation_type has a forbidden cycle
rules.action: warn_only_in_v1; published release requires exact mixed-cycle path plus explicit reviewer acknowledgement; do_not_block_without_registered_combined_constraint

rules.condition: A relation_type used by the model has no rule definition in the selected relation registry
An external_fact_claim lacks a non-not_applicable evidence_status
A model inference, hypothesis, or external fact claim is presented without enough source provenance to reproduce its basis
Review status is used as a substitute for evidence status, or evidence status is used as a substitute for human review status
Any node, edge, or condition has pending_review, rejected, disputed, or needs_reconfirmation at publication time
Any active node, edge, or condition has an unresolved reference, forbidden cycle, unknown relation rule, or unapproved exception
Any node with structural_role core, main_axis, or skeleton lacks provenance, or has a critical external claim without a supported evidence state
The exported Markdown and JSON do not identify the same immutable content revision
The release record does not pin schema version, relation rule profile/version, model revision, and change summary

A published model has any cycle warning under cycle_policy warn or any mixed-relation cycle warning, but the immutable release record lacks the exact cycle path and an explicit reviewer acknowledgement
An edge with relation_type is_evidence_for or refutes resolves to a source node with empty provenance_refs, or a target node that is not claim-bearing (entity_kind=claim or claim_kind is present)
rules.action: block_publish_and_report_edge_and_endpoint_ids; do not automatically change the target node evidence_status

notes: Published content revisions are immutable. A change creates a new draft revision; lifecycle metadata may mark the previous revision superseded in a new repository commit without rewriting the historical commit.
A semantic edit to an accepted node, edge, or condition moves that object's review_status to needs_reconfirmation.
A rejected object returns to pending_review only after a content change or newly recorded evidence; resubmitting identical content is not a valid transition.
A transition to published requires all active nodes, edges and conditions to be accepted. Evidence status remains a separate axis.

An explicit, recorded exception may override a gate only when the rule profile defines who can grant it, its scope, rationale, expiry/review condition, and audit location. No generic silent bypass is allowed.
Errors must be deterministic and point to the exact object/path.
Ordering should be stable: phase, severity, JSON pointer, then rule_id.
A validator must not modify the input as a side effect.
A missing impact path must not be reported as proof of no impact.

warning_rules: warnings must preserve stable rule IDs, involved edge IDs, cycle path, and severity
any cycle warning with a release-acknowledgement policy must be listed and acknowledged by a human decision reference
warnings must not be silently removed when exporting Markdown or downstream AI context
the release record identifies an immutable model revision; status changes create new commits and never rewrite historic content

implementation_notes: This registry is a normative draft and a specification artifact, not an executable validator.
Global ID uniqueness applies across nodes, edges, conditions, and sources, not only within each array.
VLD-106 treats conditions as conjunctive in v1. Alternative cases should use separate edges, provided their condition sets differ.
Symmetric edge reversal is covered by semantic-key normalization in VLD-106; do not implement a second, conflicting duplicate rule.
A no-path result is not evidence that the change has no effect.
A cycle marked warn may appear in a draft; publishing requires the exact warning path and an explicit reviewer acknowledgement recorded in the release record.

is_evidence_for and refutes links are between model nodes, not raw source-record IDs. Represent the sourced evidence proposition as a node with provenance_refs to one or more source records; then link that evidence node directionally to the target claim.
The evidence_status on a target claim is an aggregate human-assessed status. Adding is_evidence_for or refutes edges must not automatically upgrade or downgrade that status.
